1. **trans-Cinnamaldehyde**, \( \mathrm{C_6H_5CH{=}CHCHO} \), has **9 carbons**.
2. Methylmagnesium bromide adds a methyl group to the aldehyde, giving the allylic alcohol \( \mathrm{C_6H_5CH{=}CHCH(OH)CH_3} \): **10 carbons**.
3. PCC oxidizes this secondary alcohol to the enone \( \mathrm{C_6H_5CH{=}CHCOCH_3} \), without changing the carbon count: still **10 carbons**.
4. Dimethylsulfoxonium methylide transfers one methylene carbon to the enone (typically giving cyclopropanation; epoxidation would likewise add one carbon). Thus product 3 has \(10+1=11\) carbons.

Answer: A
